policy: per-tenant seq exactly last+1 (empty trail = 0, gaps raise SequenceGapError); compaction events must advance by EXACTLY +100 (archiver batch size), any other jump rejected; duplicate seq is a no-op (False) only on matching payload_hash, mismatch raises SequenceConflictError
bug_report: Compliance export flagged our audit trail: month-end reconciliation shows missing entries, and one incident's record differs between the primary and the replica export. A failing repro is at tests/test_regression.py. Fix append_event so the audit trail stays complete and consistent, without breaking existing behaviour.
non_guessable: decision lives in git history (a documented commit), broken by a misleading 'perf' regression commit; git log/blame is the shortcut
decision_subject: fix: enforce the audit ledger sequence contract (consecutive seq, compaction stride, hash-checked replays)
decision_rationale: The compliance findings traced to append_event accepting any increasing seq (lost messages became silent holes) and overwriting replayed events in place (how primary and replica diverged). Per-tenant seq must be exactly last_seq + 1 - an empty trail counts as last seq 0, so a tenant's first event is seq 1 - and any gap raises SequenceGapError at write time. The single exception is the archiver's compaction marker (type == 'compaction'), which must advance seq by EXACTLY 100, the archiver's documented batch size; any other jump, including +1, is rejected the same way - no tolerance knob, that turns into 'gaps allowed' within a quarter. A duplicate seq is an idempotent no-op (returns False) only when its payload_hash matches the stored event; a mismatch raises SequenceConflictError - the ledger never overwrites and never silently ignores a conflicting replay, because swallowing mismatches is how the divergence went undetected for a month.
